title: Correct flux change for A
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the change in magnetic flux for coil A as (B_initial - B_final) * π * r_A^2, yielding approximately 1.256 × 10⁻⁴ Wb.

title: Correct flux change for B
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the change in magnetic flux for coil B, using only the area within the magnetic field boundary (radius 1 cm), not the coil's full area, yielding approximately 1.256 × 10⁻⁴ Wb.

title: Correct flux change for C
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the change in magnetic flux for coil C due to rotation, using ΔΦ = B * π * r_C² * (1 - cos 30°), yielding approximately 8.4 × 10⁻⁶ Wb.

title: Applies flux definition correctly
description: Important: Student uses the formula for magnetic flux Φ = B * A * cosθ and correctly identifies the relevant area and angle for each scenario.

title: Handles boundary condition for B
description: Important: Student recognizes that for coil B, the effective area for flux calculation is limited by the circular boundary of the magnetic field, not the coil's larger radius.

title: Includes unit analysis
description: Optional: Student shows consistent unit conversion (cm to m) and reports final answers in webers (Wb).

title: Uses absolute change
description: Optional: Student correctly interprets 'how much does the magnetic flux change' as the magnitude of the change, |ΔΦ|.

title: Misinterprets area for coil B
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly uses the full area of coil B (radius 2 cm) to calculate the flux change, rather than the area within the 1 cm magnetic field boundary.

title: Sign or angle error for C
description: Pitfall: Student makes an error in the angle dependence for coil C, e.g., using sin 30° instead of (1 - cos 30°) or misapplying the dot product.
